questions.q: What is Sales Cloud's core object, the one its pipeline revolves around?
options: Opportunity
Case
Campaign
Task
questions.explain: Sales Cloud's center of gravity is the Opportunity — Leads convert into Opportunities, which move through stages to Won or Lost.

questions.q: What is Service Cloud's core object, the one customer support issues are tracked with?
options: Case
Opportunity
Lead
Account
questions.explain: Service Cloud manages customer support through Cases, tracked from open to resolved.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what questions does a typical Sales Cloud report answer?
options: Pipeline questions, like how much is in the pipeline or close rate by rep
Average time to resolve a customer issue
Case volume by support channel
Which support agents are overloaded
questions.explain: Sales Cloud reports are typically about the sales pipeline: pipeline value, close rates, stalling deals.

questions.q: Why can an analyst join Opportunity data (Sales Cloud) with Case data (Service Cloud) for the same customer?
options: Because both Clouds are built on the same core platform and share objects like Account and Contact
Because Salesforce automatically merges separate Sales Cloud and Service Cloud databases nightly
It isn't actually possible to join this data
Because Cases are secretly a type of Opportunity
questions.explain: Sales Cloud and Service Cloud aren't separate databases — they're views into the same org, sharing Account and Contact as the connecting objects.

questions.q: Why does it matter for an analyst to know whether a report is pulling from Sales Cloud or Service Cloud?
options: Because the two answer fundamentally different business questions, and mixing them up can hand a stakeholder the wrong number
It doesn't matter — Sales Cloud and Service Cloud are identical products
Because Service Cloud reports are always more accurate than Sales Cloud reports
Because only Sales Cloud data can be queried
questions.explain: A pipeline question and a support-load question are different questions entirely — knowing which Cloud a report draws from tells you what it actually measures.
